data.content_ref: inline:Under the 'demand a causal mechanism' stance, the target fails to provide a causal mechanism for the evidence distinction required by the problem. The problem asks what evidence within a single evaluation distinguishes a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. While the target provides a causal mechanism for why the expert might be more reliable (tool-dependency blindness causing catastrophic failures on out-of-scope variables), it provides no causal mechanism for how an evaluator would operationally distinguish a genuine reliability gain from coincidental compliance within a single evaluation. It omits the exact causal proof demanded by the stance.
